content: The user prefers concise answers first, with optional detail only when it helps make a decision.
The user prefers code examples that are complete and runnable rather than abbreviated pseudocode.
The user prefers planning before implementation for changes that touch more than one module.
The user does not want AI attribution in commit messages unless explicitly requested.
The user prefers uv for Python dependency management and does not want pip or poetry used in this repository.
The user prefers feature branches and does not commit directly to the main branch.
For Rust builds in this repository, use the rebuild-and-update-install script instead of cargo install directly.
The user wants tests run after a logical commit so failures can be tied to a known checkpoint.
The user prefers local-first tools for personal data and wants cloud services to be opt-in.
The user wants destructive operations to show a clear confirmation step and a recovery path.
The personal agent should ask before sending messages, deleting files, or making purchases.
The user prefers dates in ISO 8601 format when they are used in logs or exported data.
The user prefers Markdown documentation with short headings and command examples.
The user dislikes recurring notifications that do not include a concrete action or decision.
The agent should distinguish durable personal facts from temporary session context before saving memory.
The agent should store a user's stable preference in the global namespace rather than a project namespace.
Project-specific implementation decisions belong in the project namespace and should include the project name.
The user prefers the assistant to state uncertainty instead of inventing missing details.
The user prefers a short daily briefing at 08:00 local time on weekdays only.
The user's timezone for personal reminders is America/New_York.
The user blocks focused work from 09:00 to 11:30 on weekdays and does not want meetings scheduled there.
The user prefers travel itineraries that include buffer time between connections rather than the shortest possible route.
The user is vegetarian but eats eggs and dairy; restaurant recommendations should respect this.
The user prefers metric units for cooking and weather, but accepts miles for running routes.
The user wants health-related reminders phrased as options and never as diagnoses.
The user prefers grocery lists grouped by store section instead of sorted alphabetically.
The user keeps an emergency contact named Morgan and does not want that contact exposed in public outputs.
The user prefers notifications on Signal for urgent personal matters and email for non-urgent summaries.
The user's weekly review happens on Sunday evening and covers calendar, finances, and open tasks.
The user wants the agent to summarize long email threads before asking which action to take.
The user decided that Redis is the session cache with a five-minute TTL for the personal-agent gateway.
The personal-agent gateway uses SQLite for local configuration and LibSQL for memory storage.
The memory service exposes standard MCP JSON-RPC over stdio so Hermes can start it as a subprocess.
Hermes should call the memory context tool at the start of a session before attempting a multi-step task.
Durable decisions are saved only after the agent has separated them from conversational filler.
A memory recall response should include source identifiers so the agent can cite or update the original entry.
The MCP server logs diagnostics to stderr and reserves stdout exclusively for JSON-RPC responses.
The personal agent runs without an Anthropic API key for core remember, recall, list, and graph operations.
Optional LLM enrichment may use an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, but storage must degrade gracefully when it is unavailable.
The default personal-agent namespace is global for stable preferences and project:personal-agent for system decisions.
The agent should use a bounded context budget when injecting memories into a Hermes prompt.
Context assembly should prefer a small number of high-confidence memories over filling every available token.
Chit-chat such as greetings and thanks should skip the memory retrieval round trip.
Questions about the user's preferences should be rewritten with explicit user-context wording before retrieval.
Procedural questions beginning with how should be treated as skill-oriented retrieval requests.
The agent should prefer a held-out retrieval set when evaluating ranking changes instead of trusting one development set.
Memory evaluation queries must not be embedded as special cases or copied into production ranking logic.
The retrieval benchmark reports both Hit@k and mean reciprocal rank so one lucky top result is not enough.
A retrieval experiment is kept only when correctness checks pass and held-out quality does not regress materially.
The user chose local fastembed models for semantic search to keep personal memories on the machine.
The embedding model cache lives under the user's local cache directory and should not be committed to git.
Keyword search uses FTS5 with stemming so related word forms can match without a network service.
Graph expansion is useful for connected project decisions but should not overwhelm a direct semantic match.
Recent memories may break ties, but recency must not outrank a strong semantic match solely because it is new.
Importance scores are a tie-breaker that reflect durable value, not a substitute for query relevance.
A failed embedding request should be visible to the caller rather than silently returning unranked keyword results.
The retrieval API returns an empty result for an empty namespace rather than falling back to unrelated projects.
Memory records are grouped into topic directories with L0 abstracts, L1 overviews, and L2 details.
L0 memory abstracts are capped at 256 characters so they are cheap to use during hierarchical navigation.
L1 memory overviews are used for reranking and planning while L2 content is loaded on demand.
The context assembler fills breadth-first tiers under a token budget and keeps the final prompt deterministic.
The hierarchy uses deterministic topic paths so rebuilding the same memories does not create noisy rewrites.
The agent should record retrieval trajectories when debugging why a hierarchical result was selected.
The user keeps source code for personal automations in a private GitHub repository with protected main.
Pull requests for personal automations need a summary, test evidence, and a rollback note.
The user's home lab runs Debian hosts and uses Tailscale for private access between machines.
Home lab services are deployed with Docker Compose and backed up nightly to an encrypted external disk.
The backup policy retains seven daily snapshots and four weekly snapshots before pruning older data.
The user wants backup failures reported immediately, but successful backup notifications batched into the daily briefing.
The user tracks household spending by category and reviews subscriptions once per month.
The agent must never approve a bank transfer or financial purchase without explicit confirmation in the current conversation.
Tax documents are stored in a local encrypted folder organized by tax year.
The user prefers a plain-text export of financial reminders rather than a spreadsheet attachment.
The user's preferred running days are Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday mornings.
The user is training for a half marathon and prefers gradual mileage increases with a recovery week every fourth week.
The user wants exercise reminders skipped when the calendar has a full-day travel event.
The user plans international trips around one carry-on bag and prefers trains over short regional flights.
For flights, the user prefers an aisle seat and avoids overnight departures when alternatives are reasonable.
The agent should save hotel booking confirmation numbers but not store full payment card details.
The user enjoys science fiction novels, documentary podcasts, and cooperative strategy games.
Book recommendations should avoid books the user has already marked as finished in the reading log.
The user prefers podcast recommendations under forty-five minutes on weekday mornings.
The user's smart-home lights should turn on gradually at sunset and turn off at the household bedtime.
The smart thermostat target is 20 degrees Celsius during the day and 17 degrees Celsius overnight.
The agent should not unlock doors or disarm the home alarm from a text-only request.
The user keeps a small balcony herb garden with basil, mint, thyme, and rosemary.
Watering reminders for the herb garden should be postponed when the weather forecast predicts rain.
The user prefers quiet hours from 22:00 to 07:00 and does not want non-urgent agent notifications then.
The user wants important deadlines surfaced three days ahead and again on the morning they are due.
The user prefers task lists sorted by urgency first, then by estimated effort.
Tasks that require another person's response should be labeled waiting rather than repeatedly resurfaced as overdue.
The agent should ask one focused clarification question when a task has multiple plausible interpretations.
For long-running work, the agent should provide a progress update at meaningful checkpoints instead of frequent noise.
The user prefers failures to include the command that failed, the likely cause, and the next recovery step.
The user wants secrets loaded from an encrypted store or environment variable and never printed in logs.
Personal-agent logs should redact API keys, tokens, email addresses, and full file paths when exported.
The agent should use read-only access when researching a new service before it is allowed to mutate data.
MCP tools should be enabled using an explicit allowlist rather than exposing every server tool by default.
Delegated agent tasks should have a bounded scope, a written deliverable, and an explicit timeout.
Parallel agent work is safe only when each worker has an isolated worktree or disjoint files.
The user prefers the primary agent to review delegated changes before merging them into the active branch.
Hermes Bot profiles should have separate memory namespaces when they represent different roles.
Cron automations should include a timeout, a delivery target, and a way to disable the job without editing code.
A recurring personal-agent job should be idempotent so retrying after a timeout does not duplicate side effects.
The user prefers browser automation to save a screenshot or URL evidence for important completed actions.
Web research should record publication dates and distinguish primary sources from summaries.
The user prefers research answers to separate verified facts, reasonable inferences, and open questions.
When a source conflicts with an existing memory, the agent should keep both until the conflict is resolved explicitly.
The user wants stale memories reviewed before archival rather than silently deleted.
Memory consolidation should merge duplicates only when the durable meaning is preserved and provenance remains visible.
The user's preferred first step for a broken automation is to inspect recent logs before changing configuration.
The user prefers a dry-run mode for scripts that could modify more than ten records.
The agent should preserve the original user wording when storing a nuanced preference or boundary.
The user wants session summaries to record decisions, unresolved questions, and next actions separately.
A session summary should omit transient greetings, repeated tool output, and credentials.
